failure.title: Standard performance corpus used a non-contract constraint-detail key
failure.note: The first fresh-owned performance smoke retained its structured HTTP 500 failure, complete environment and corpus identity, teardown transcript, and empty container, volume, and network inventories. Fresh no-cache images and the exact 50-client corpus succeeded before the first client-detail warm-up failed, so no measurement began and cleanup completed exactly.
failure.diagnosis: The direct-SQL standard corpus stored a preference constraint detail under the strict-invalid key preference instead of the canonical nullable note field. Client-detail output validation rejected the persisted shape and returned sanitized HTTP 500. The failure path also omitted bounded response diagnostics and pre-cleanup Compose logs that would have made the product cause directly attributable before database and container teardown.

rawEvidence.policy: Raw captures remain immutable in the developer-local vault; this public summary retains reviewed failure facts and cryptographic provenance without publishing browser traces, videos, logs, or mutation payloads.
